title: Model: the Gaussian mode u = (1/q) exp(-ik r^2/2q), q = z + i z_R, solves the paraxial equation; its 1/q, Gouy and waist relations check
statement: In the paraxial model, u(r, z) = (1/q) exp(-i k r^2/(2q)) with q = z + i z_R and z_R = pi w0^2/lambda satisfies (1/r) d_r(r d_r u) - 2ik d_z u = 0; 1/q = 1/R(z) - i lambda/(pi w(z)^2) with w(z)^2 = w0^2 (1 + z^2/z_R^2) and R(z) = z (1 + z_R^2/z^2); i z_R/q = (w0/w) exp(i arctan(z/z_R)); w(0) = w0, w(z)/z tends to lambda/(pi w0); and w(z) = w0 (1 + z^2/(2 z_R^2)) + O(z^4) near the waist.
holds_when: Model, not a measurement: scalar paraxial Gaussian beam in free space, field u e^{i(omega t - kz)}, k = 2 pi/lambda, w the 1/e^2 intensity radius; z, w0, lambda > 0. Checked by SymPy 1.14.0 with mpmath 1.3.0 and pint 0.24.4 under the formalize-derivation helper 0.1.0 (mutation set m0.1); the verdict of each step is in the output. Textbook material, recorded as the skill's worked example.
